$comment: Toyota 1JZ-GTE (2.5-litre turbo JZ). Researched 2026-09-29. Two variants: the 1990-1996 parallel twin-turbo (CT12A, 8.5:1, fixed cam timing; JZA70, JZX81, JZX90, early JZZ30) and the 1996-2006 VVT-i single turbo (CT15B, 9.0:1; JZZ30, JZX100, JZS171, JZX110, JZX110W). Primary sources: Toyota's own catalogue data (toyota.jp used-car catalogue and goo-net grade pages for every chassis), Toyota's 2001 Chaser brochure, Toyota's September 1996 JZX100 repair book (English machine translation on archive.org: boost, oil capacity, gearboxes, shims, intercooler removal) and Toyota's parts catalogue (japan-parts.eu mirror: every oil pan part number and sump position, rods, pistons, heads). Missing or weak: no Toyota engine weight or outline dimensions (both estimated), no Toyota statement of crank/rod/piston materials, no twin-turbo boost or intercooler position, no injector size per generation, no VVT-i cam specs, no ECU part numbers.

bellhousing.note: Engine-side pattern shared by 1JZ and 2JZ. Factory gearboxes behind the 1JZ-GTE: Toyota R154 5-speed (JZA70, JZZ30, JZX90, JZX100, JZX110; Toyota repair book model list, PDF p. 5: R154 (5M/T) E-JZX100-ATMVZ, A341E (4A/T ECT-iE) E-JZX100-ATPVZ) and Aisin 4-speed automatics: the A341E on the JZX100 (repair book), a 4-speed ECT-S on the JZX81 (toyota.jp does not name the model). The JZX81 GT Twin Turbo was automatic only (goo-net lists 4AT only). Toyota parts catalogue: the manual-gearbox flywheel 13405-46030 (8 bolts, 90910-02103) is the same part on the JZX90 (1992-10 to 1996-09), JZX100 (1996-09 on) and JZX110 (2000-10 to 2002-10), so the flywheel did not change with VVT-i. The R154 clutch housing (bellhousing) is also one part, 31111-14110, on the JZX90 and JZX100 (the ESB part list calls it the 1JZ R154 bellhousing), and the starter is the same on both (28100-46130, 12 V 0.8 kW; 28100-46140, 1.4 kW, cold-climate). So twin-turbo and VVT-i engines take the same bellhousing, flywheel and starter behind an R154; the automatic bellhousings (A340E/A341E) were not compared.

sources.note: '500-550whp is pretty close to maxing out a 1JZ-GTE with stock internals. Without additional high-flow head work, forged internals, valve springs, and a performance head gasket, pushing any more power than that is very risky and unsustainable.'

value.note: Upper end of the quoted 500-550 whp range. The same article also says 'Maintaining stock internals, it is possible to hit numbers around 700 horsepower with some heavier duty equipment', so its ceiling is loose.

reportedLimits.context: Tuning-guide article (8020 Automotive), not a measured failure test: assumes E85 tuning, upgraded fuel system (twin pumps), a large single turbo and a proper tune on a healthy engine; beyond about 550 whp it recommends forged internals, head work, valve springs and a performance head gasket. No engine builder with a named test car was found.

sources.note: Question: 'The engine will be running E85 and aiming for around the 650 horsepower mark'; Andre Simon (Tutor): '650 hp on a stock 1JZ should be very achievable, particularly on a quality fuel like E85.' ... 'Detontaion is the usual killer of these engines when modified'.

value.note: Neither post says crank or wheel horsepower; stored as crank-power, the more conservative reading.

reportedLimits.context: Opinion of an established tuning educator (HP Academy tutor), not a test: VVT-i 1JZ-GTE, stock bottom end including rod bolts, E85 fuel, good tune; he names detonation, not the parts, as the usual cause of failure. No rpm limit was given.

variants.notes: Manual and automatic ratings are identical. Gearboxes: R154 5-speed (JZZ30, JZX100 Tourer V, JZX110 iR-V, Verossa VR25) or 4-speed automatic (A341E on the JZX100 per Toyota's repair book; the Crown Athlete V, Blit iR-V and Cresta Roulant G were automatic only). Hardware changes versus the twin turbo, from Toyota's parts catalogue: new cylinder head (11101-88400 to 11101-88410), head gasket (11115-88400 to 11115-88410), pistons (13101-88400 to 13101-88410) and camshafts (13501/13502-88400 to 13501-88410 / 13502-88401); the connecting rods (13201-46030), rod bolts and manual flywheel (13405-46030) carry over. The valvetrain stays shim-over-bucket: Toyota's JZX100 repair book replaces shims from above with a lifter press (SST 09248-05410/05420) and says 'Install the shim with the coated part (gold side) facing up. (Excluding 2JZ-GE)'; the new shims (13753-46030 on) come in 0.02 mm steps from 2.50 mm. Cam specifications for the VVT-i engine were not found. Oil capacity 5.4 L with filter is the JZX100 figure (top-level oilCapacity).
